common_name: North American Riparian Willow Fly (X-4 Chromosome Fusion & Red/Brown Puparia)

evolutionary_history.note: All three chronospecies are extant (0 Ma). Predecessor and successor are the campaign chronoseries neighbors, not literal ancestors.

what_changes_at_this_scale.statement: At the 2.117 µm detail scale the Turing wavelength is buffered relative to the primordium-scale tergite stripe. Body-length scaling with exponent beta = 0.35 (subcellular pigment-cell diffusion) replaces the much larger primordium-scale wavelength ratios of the sibling slots.

primordium_scale_sibling_wavelength_m.source: Existing MorphoEval slots, not refit here: miller-drosophila-affinis-turing-wavelength (96 µm class), wittkopp-drosophila-americana-turing-wavelength (139 µm), clark-drosophila-ananassae-turing-wavelength (85 µm).

what_changes_at_this_scale.x4_fusion_and_puparium: The X–4 fusion and red/brown puparium diagnose D. americana among virilis-group flies. They are not parameters of the reaction-diffusion system. At this scale they do not multiply the inhibitor range by the tergite-stripe factor; activator diffusivity Du carries the buffered wavelength shift at a shared diffusion ratio r.

equations.kinetics: Schnakenberg cubic activator-inhibitor in the Gierer–Meinhardt class: f = a - u + u^2 v, g = b - u^2 v
equations.onset_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)
equations.maximum_growth: k_sigma = argmax_k sigma_+(k), where sigma_+ is the larger eigenvalue of J - k^2 D
equations.turing_discriminant: (D_v f_u + D_u g_v)^2 - 4 D_u D_v det(J) > 0 and D_v f_u + D_u g_v > 0
equations.equal_diffusion_ablation: D_u = D_v (r = 1) violates D_v f_u + D_u g_v > 0 for this Jacobian

parameters.r_note: r = D_v / D_u = 10 lies just above the onset ratio r_c ≈ 8.57 for this Jacobian, so the expressed wavelength stays close to the critical wavelength k_c.
parameters.domain: periodic square patch of ocellar pigment epithelium; physical pixel size is set so the linear-theory wavelength of maximum growth equals 2.117 µm

empirical_claims: Wittkopp et al. (2009) showed that abdominal pigmentation divergence between dark D. americana and light D. novamexicana is genetic and largely cis-regulatory. That result is a millimetre-scale color difference, not a measurement of a 2.117 µm wavelength.

Turing (1952) and Murray (1981) give the critical wavenumber k_c selected by a two-species reaction-diffusion system. This slot identifies the assigned 2.117 µm detail scale with the expressed ocellar pigment wavelength of that dispersion relation.

Clark et al. (2007) sequenced D. ananassae among the twelve Drosophila genomes. O'Grady and DeSalle (2018) place americana in the virilis radiation and affinis and ananassae in Sophophora. The chronoseries comparison uses those placements plus the buffered-Du hypothesis; it does not claim a fossil sequence.

specimen.provenance: Repository species card for Drosophila americana. Wikimedia Commons searches on 2026-10-27 returned no CC photograph of D. americana (hits were D. melanogaster plates and an unrelated PDF), so the gallery card is the vendored specimen image.
specimen.what_it_shows: Brown low-frequency spiral/target pigment card with a printed species caption and a 100 µm scale bar. It is not a transmission electron micrograph of the ocellus.
specimen.license: Repository species-gallery asset used as the canonical comparison image for this taxon.
